title: runtime/kv: refactor KV cache allocator behind BlockMap abstraction (no behavior change)
author: Samir Qureshi
description: Motivation: Follow-on work for KV cache compaction requires a representation that can (eventually) support movable blocks / remapping while keeping the decode fast path tight. The current allocator logic is spread across a few structs and requires callers to reason about layout/ownership details. This PR refactors the KV cache allocator internals behind a `BlockMap` abstraction (segment/page oriented), without changing allocation policy or observable behavior. This is intended as a pure refactor to unblock the compaction engine work (separate PRs) and to make scheduler integration points explicit. Scope: - Introduce `BlockMap` + `BlockHandle` types as the canonical mapping from logical (sequence_id, layer, head, block_idx) to physical device offsets - Centralize allocation/free bookkeeping in `BlockMap` with a narrow interface used by the KV cache manager - Keep existing block size, eviction behavior, and admission control unchanged - Add focused unit tests for mapping correctness and invariants (alignment, bounds, reuse) - Add lightweight debug-only validation hooks (guarded by runtime flag) to aid compaction bring-up later Non-goals: - No compaction/moves in this PR - No changes to kernel address math (still uses the same computed offsets) - No changes to eviction policy or scheduler decisions Notes on performance: The fast path remains a couple of inlined calls and pointer arithmetic; the refactor mostly reorganizes metadata. I ran the microbench locally and internal perf suite jobs show within-noise deltas (see CI artifacts). Checklist: [x] No behavior change (validated by allocator golden tests + perf suite) [x] Added/updated unit tests [x] Added debug assertions behind flag [x] Updated internal comments on ownership/thread-safety Related: ENG-2844 (allocator refactor), compaction engine PR will build on this; metrics PR (18423) lands separately.
commits: runtime/kv: introduce BlockMap interface + core data structures
runtime/kv: migrate KvCacheAllocator to use BlockMap internally
tests/runtime: add blockmap mapping/allocator invariant tests
runtime/kv: add debug-only validation + stats hooks (no export yet)
cleanup: remove duplicated helpers + tighten comments on thread-safety
ci_summary: Checks: build (linux-gpu) PASS; unit-tests PASS; runtime-tests PASS; lint PASS; clang-tidy PASS; perf-suite (nightly sample) PASS. Notes: one transient runner failure on linux-gpu build was re-run (see 2025-02-22 update) and passed.
conversation: Noah Patel (review): Can you clarify the invariants around BlockHandle stability? If we later do compaction, we’ll need to ensure callers don’t stash raw offsets. Samir Qureshi (author): Yep—added a comment + renamed a couple APIs to emphasize handles are opaque and offsets are computed on demand; current callers only use `GetDevicePtr()` within the kernel launch path. Omar El-Sayed (review): Please add a golden test that alloc/free patterns preserve the exact same block reuse order as before; we don’t want accidental eviction/placement drift. Samir Qureshi: Added `kv_cache_allocator_golden_test` which replays the previous allocator sequence and asserts identical block indices and free-list behavior. Grace Kim (review): Concern: debug validation might add overhead if accidentally enabled in prod. Can we hard-gate with both compile-time and runtime flag? Samir Qureshi: Done—validation code is compiled in but early-exits behind `--runtime_kv_debug_validate_blockmap` and also uses `RW_DEBUG` to keep checks out of release builds where possible. Hiro Tanaka (review): Please confirm kernel address math is unchanged; any offset unit mismatch would be catastrophic but subtle. Samir Qureshi: Verified by diffing computed offsets in a targeted test that compares old/new paths; also kept the same `BytesPerBlock` constants and alignment. Sofia Ivanova (review): Any new lock ordering? Scheduler sometimes calls into KV manager on hot paths; I want to avoid surprises. Samir Qureshi: No new locks; BlockMap reuses existing allocator mutex and keeps lock scope the same. Added a short section in README on thread-safety and lock ownership. Approvals: Noah Patel approved (2025-02-24); Omar El-Sayed approved (2025-02-24); Grace Kim approved with comment resolved (2025-02-23); Hiro Tanaka approved (2025-02-23); Sofia Ivanova approved (2025-02-24). Merged via squash into main (2025-02-24).
release_notes: Internal-only refactor: KV cache allocator now uses BlockMap abstraction to prepare for future compaction work; no user-visible behavior changes expected.
